summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and COPD, was admitted for hypoxia, somnolence, and cough productive of green sputum. She was found to have MRSA pneumonia and a suspected ESBL-producing Klebsiella urinary tract infection, leading to sepsis. She required ICU care for hypotension and hypoxia, managed with vasopressors, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and respiratory support. A central line was placed in the ED, later replaced with a PICC for outpatient antibiotic therapy. Her mental status fluctuated due to CO2 retention and over-sedation from home medications, prompting dose reductions in baclofen, pregabalin, and discontinuation of oxybutynin. She improved with treatment, was weaned to room air, and discharged home on IV Vancomycin and Ertapenem with nursing support.
